title: Longshore drift diagram sheet
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y8 lesson 3 (Longshore drift diagram sheet (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 3: What work do the waves do? Erosion, transport, deposition and longshore drift (4.2). To understand how waves erode, transport and deposit material along the coast

picture.draw: Draw and label: Longshore drift diagram sheet

questions.q: Explain longshore drift in three steps.
questions.a: Swash carries sediment up the beach at an angle; backwash pulls it straight down; it zigzags along the coast
questions.model: Step 1: the wind makes waves arrive at an angle. Step 2: swash pushes sediment up at that angle. Step 3: backwash drags it straight down, so it moves along.

questions.a: Water and air forced into cracks, breaking the rock
When they lose energy, for example in sheltered bays

questions.q: Core: Draw a labelled diagram of longshore drift with the prevailing wind, swash, backwash and direction of movement.
questions.a: Diagram with angled swash arrows, straight backwash arrows, zigzag path and wind arrow
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: wind arrow from the south-west, swash arrow up at an angle, backwash straight down, then the next swash.

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, explain how erosion, transport and deposition link along one stretch of coast.
questions.a: Cliffs are eroded; material is moved along by longshore drift; it is deposited where waves lose energy, forming beaches

questions.q: Stretch: Why do chalk cliffs suffer from solution?
questions.a: Chalk is a form of calcium carbonate that slowly dissolves in slightly acidic sea water

questions.q: Material bouncing along the sea bed is moved by:
Big question: how can a pebble from Dorset end up miles along the coast?
questions.a: Longshore drift moves it along in a zigzag as waves hit the beach at an angle
